simple.meaning: זָנָב (zânâb) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “the tail (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 4:4. The surrounding context includes family line, commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָנָב (H2180) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: זָנָב (zânâb) / H2180 is traced through Exodus 4:4, Deuteronomy 28:13, Deuteronomy 28:44, Judges 15:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand, and take it by the tail.”

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand, and take it by the tail.”

Yahweh will make you the head, and not the tail. You will be above only, and you will not be beneath, if you listen to the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you today, to observe and to do,
He will lend to you, and you won’t lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.

Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.
He moves his tail like a cedar.

Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them,
Therefore Yahweh will cut off from Israel head and tail,
Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.

definitions.full: H2180. zanab זָנָב noun masculine Judg 15:4 tail , also (figurative) end, stump (Late Hebrew id. , Assyrian zibbatu Hom NS 368 , Ethiopic Arabic , Aramaic , דַּנְבָּא דּוּנְבָּא, ) — ׳ז absolute 15:4 (twice in verse) + 5 t.; suffix זְנָבוֺ Job 40:17 ; plural זְנָבוֺת Judg 15:4 ; construct זַנְבוֺת Isa 7:4 ; — 1. a. tail of fox Judg 15:4 (3 t. in verse), of serpent Exod 4:4 (J), of hippopotamus Job 40:17 ; b. figurative of common people, opposed to rulers Isa 9:13 ; 19:15 (in both, וְזָנָב ראֹשׁ , || וְאַגְמוֺן כִּמָּה ; 9:14 is incorrect gloss); of subject-people (opposed to ראֹשׁ ) Deut 28:13 , 44 . 2 end, stump (of firebrand, אוּד ) in metaphor Isa 7:4 .
definitions.rootNote: from 2179 (in the original sense of flapping );
